analysis: Examined the three changed files. (1) StartCommand+Picker.swift: pickerLoadBudgetGiB and modelFitsBudget (lines 87-93) now delegate to AutopilotBuildEligibility.loadBudgetGiB and fitsLoadBudget. The base inline logic was: finite check, memoryGb in (0, 4096], UnifiedMemoryCap hard cap minus load headroom, and a sizeGb finite and positive check. The delegate's source is not supplied, so I cannot confirm it keeps the same bounds and NaN/inf rejection. This is a local picker UX and sizing guard against OOM, not a trust boundary or auth control. It affects only availability on the provider (T-016/T-029 class), and the loader rechecks live memory, so I see no concrete security regression. A later pass should verify that the delegate retains the finite and positive guards and the modelIDs-based reserve. (2) AutopilotDownloadCommandTests.swift is a new test file covering autopilot downloads CLI enable/disable, limit parsing and consent non-modification. It asserts that modelAutopilot consent state is untouched. It has no production code and no security impact. The production Autopilot.Downloads commands are not in this batch. Their storage and model limits are a disk-fill/availability concern (T-016) and need review where implemented. (3) ScheduledWindowSelectionTests.swift adds a test that cached autopilot builds carry into the next window only while their weight hash still matches, are dropped if rewritten or vanished, and are not carried without recorded consent. This is a positive test of integrity re-verification, relevant to T-012/T-027 (weight substitution). The production ScheduledWindowSelection.noteAutopilotCachedBuilds logic is not supplied, so I cannot confirm its re-hash and consent gating. No findings; the open question is whether the unseen production implementations match these tests and the delegate.
